value.body: Banks use analytics teams for credit risk, fraud detection, customer segmentation, collections and regulatory reporting. In public-sector banks these jobs are usually filled through specialist recruitment or by moving officers into analytics and risk departments; private banks and fintechs hire analysts more directly. A BBA can be a starting point, but most analytics roles also expect data skills.

items.label: Typical work
items.value: Credit risk, fraud, customer and portfolio analytics, MIS reporting

items.label: Public-sector routes
items.value: Bank PO/clerk entry, then internal moves; specialist officer drives

items.label: Public sector banks
items.note: Alongside 21 private sector banks, per the same report
items.source: RBI Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India

items.label: IBPS specialist officer posts (CRP SPL-XIV)
items.note: Across IT, law, marketing, HR, agriculture and Rajbhasha officer posts; no separate analytics post

value.title: How you get in
value.body: For public-sector banks, the main route for a BBA graduate is the officer or clerk exam (IBPS PO/Clerk, SBI PO/Clerk), followed by postings in risk or analytics departments. Specialist-officer posts in data science or risk typically ask for a postgraduate degree, certifications or experience. RBI's statistics-side posts ask for a master's in a quantitative subject.

value.title: At a glance
items: Skills in Excel, SQL, a statistics or programming tool and basic credit concepts matter more than the degree title.
Specialist-officer notifications in analytics are irregular and have few posts.
Private banks, NBFCs and analytics firms hire more analysts than public-sector banks do.
An MBA or a quantitative master's widens later options.
